text:
sophia: Hey team — I’m getting set up and hitting a kube access wall. I can see the cluster but not the redwood-dev namespace. Trying to kubectl logs and port-forward for the local dev server. Any quick RBAC or kubeconfig tweaks I should ask for?

it-ops: welcome, sophia :wave: what does `kubectl config current-context` show for you? also which email/username did you sign up with so we can look up the SSO mapping.

sophia: current-context is `redwood-gke-us-central1`. Signed up with sophia@redwood.ai. I can list namespaces but `kubectl get pods -n redwood-dev` returns `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden`

jamal: that looks like a role permission issue. We usually give new devs a serviceAccount-based kubeconfig for the first week (scoped to team namespace + port-forward/logs). Want me to create a short-lived binding for you? If so I need your kubernetes username (k8s principal) or I can bind the crew:sophia AD group if you’re in it.

maria: hey sophia, welcome to infra! for context, the team namespace is `teams/maria-products` (alias redwood-dev). We allow port-forward and logs for devs but not exec into prod pods. jamal — binding to the AD group is fine if it’s easier.

it-ops: tagging the usual runbook steps: 1) confirm identity 2) create a namespace-limited rolebinding 3) provide a kubeconfig snippet pointing at a service account. Example RBAC we use (run as admin):

```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: dev-namespace-ops
  namespace: teams/maria-products
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","pods/log","services","endpoints"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch","create","delete"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods/portforward"]
  verbs: ["create"]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: onboarding-sophia
  namespace: teams/maria-products
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: onboarding-sophia-binding
  namespace: teams/maria-products
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: onboarding-sophia
  namespace: teams/maria-products
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: dev-namespace-ops
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

it-ops: once we create that SA we mint a kubeconfig like: `kubectl config set-credentials onboarding-sophia --token=<TOKEN>` and then `kubectl config set-context onboarding-sophia-context --cluster=redwood-gke-us-central1 --user=onboarding-sophia --namespace=teams/maria-products` — we then share the kubeconfig file over the secure onboarding ticket.

jamal: I can do the Role + SA now for sophia@redwood.ai. do you want the token or we can add you to the `devs-maria` AD group (longer-term)?

sophia: token is fine for now, thanks. Quick Q: will this let me port-forward to localhost:3000 for the dev server?

maria: yes — port-forwarding is allowed in dev namespace. watch out that port 3000 conflicts on your laptop.

onboard-bot: Ticket #ONB-482 created — request: kube namespace access for sophia, assignee: jamal, ETA: 2 hours.

jamal: done — created SA `onboarding-sophia` and RoleBinding. I uploaded the kubeconfig to the ticket. Token is rotated and expires in 7 days. Please confirm you can `kubectl get pods -n teams/maria-products` and `kubectl port-forward svc/dev-server 3000:80 -n teams/maria-products`.

sophia: confirmed — `kubectl get pods -n teams/maria-products` returns pods and `kubectl port-forward` works. Thanks everyone! :tada:

maria: welcome aboard, sophia. ping me if you need app creds or local env vars.

it-ops: leaving a short note in the runbook to prefer ServiceAccount kubeconfigs for first-week access (helps with audit logs).
